Subject: Re: Discovery - FastRetail inference requirements

Thanks for the call today - quick recap from our side.

Key goals: reduce perceived latency for our customer-facing chat widget and support streaming product descriptions for search results. Our current vendor has average TTFT ~800ms which feels sluggish on mobile.

Rough targets we discussed:
- TTFT target: <= 200ms P50, <= 350ms P95 for production traffic
- Streaming cadence: small chunks every ~200-400ms to keep tokens appearing smoothly on mobile
- Concurrency: support ~120 concurrent active users on peak region (US-West) per instance; aggregate peak regional concurrency ~1.2k across cluster
- Throughput profile: bursts of short requests (<=60 tokens) during promotional events, steady mid-size requests (200-500 tokens) during catalog generation

Open items for us: can you confirm Redwood's recommended approach for streaming (SSE vs WebSocket) and whether there are any limits/recommendations on chunk size and cadence? Also need a rough cost estimate for Dedicated pool sizing that meets these concurrency and TTFT targets.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Search Experience
FastRetail

Alex / Marissa - looping in Jonas (runtime) and following up with some technical notes ahead of the validation call. I ran a quick back-of-envelope mapping from your targets to recommended configs.

Quick answers up front:
- Streaming: SSE works fine and is simplest to integrate; WebSocket gives marginally lower overhead at high concurrency but requires additional connection management. We support both in our SDKs. For mobile, SSE + small chunks is a good default.
- Chunk cadence & sizing: recommend aiming for 150-300ms cadence with 8-40 token chunks for conversational workloads. For longer generation (catalog items), larger chunks (50-150 tokens) at 250-400ms cadence reduce overhead and improve throughput.
- TTFT: TTFT budgets depend on model size + quantization + KV cache hit rates. For a Llama2-13B optimized path with 4-bit quant and warm KV cache, 150-250ms P50 is attainable; P95 below 350ms is achievable with Dedicated pool sizing + smart routing.
- Concurrency/throughput: to hit ~120 active users per instance with mixed workloads, recommend Dedicated pool with 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (model/quantization dependent) per cluster node and autoscaling headroom for 1.5x burst. We'll provide a more precise estimate once we see a representative token/sec distribution.

Proposed test plan (high-level):
1) Baseline TTFT test: single-instance cold and warm runs, measure P50/P95 for 100, 400, 800-token sequences.
2) Streaming cadence test: run simulated mobile clients at 150ms, 250ms, 400ms chunk cadence and measure perceived latency & reorder issues.
3) Concurrency stress: synthetic clients to reach 120 concurrent active sessions per instance and measure TTFT and token throughput.

What we need from you for an accurate sizing/cost:
- Realistic traffic mix (fraction of short vs mid vs long requests) and avg tokens per request
- Acceptable fallback behavior for transient degradation (e.g., degrade to non-streaming or fallback model variant)

I'll prepare a short lab checklist and an updated sizing proposal ahead of the call. Marissa - I'm available Tue 10am PST or Wed 9am PST for the technical validation.

- Dylan
